useCase.summary: AI assistant that reads store orders and products so it can review them for merchants. Read-only access is enough.

verdict.headline: You can connect a development store within hours. Production on merchant stores needs protected customer data approval and Shopify App Store review, and Shopify documents no turnaround time.
verdict.startToday: Create the Dev Dashboard app and file the protected customer data request now. Shopify's review is the slowest step and cannot start until the request is filed, the compliance webhooks are in place and the app is submitted. Protected customer data cannot be requested once the app is under review.

composio.why: The Composio toolkit exists but lists no managed auth schemes and no managed scopes, so you need your own Shopify app. Use the Composio callback URL as its redirect URI. Composio's metadata lists write_orders as required for the orders tool. Read access is enough for this use case, so request read_orders instead.

requirements.item: A Shopify account with app development permissions and a Dev Dashboard app (a Partner account is needed for the Partner Dashboard steps in production; whether creating the app needs one is unconfirmed)
Public distribution selected for the app (needed to serve merchants beyond your own store)
Protected customer data access approved for the order data you read, justified as the minimum needed
App icon, API contact details and an emergency developer contact
A development store to install and test the app
A Composio custom auth config holding your Shopify client ID and secret

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard and choose public distribution
steps.detail: Sign in to the Dev Dashboard with an account that has app development permissions and create an app. On the app's Home, open the Distribution card and select Public distribution if merchants other than you will install it. The choice is permanent, so confirm it first.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI and scopes
steps.detail: In the app's settings in the Dev Dashboard, or in the [auth] section of shopify.app.toml, add the redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Declare the scopes read_orders and read_products. Do not add read_all_orders unless you need orders older than 60 days.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access
steps.detail: In the Partner Dashboard, open the app's API access requests and request protected customer data. Request only the fields the assistant needs. Fields such as name, address, phone or email are Level 2 and need individual approval. Complete the Data protection details. Do this before submitting the app, because it cannot be requested while the app is under review.

steps.title: Connect a development store through Composio
steps.detail: Create a Composio custom auth config for the shopify toolkit with your app's client ID and secret. Install the app on a development store. After the install, check the granted scopes in the token response, since merchants can edit them on the authorize screen. Run SHOPIFY_LIST_ORDERS and SHOPIFY_GET_PRODUCTS. Apps installed only on development stores can use customer data without a review.

steps.title: Prepare App Store submission requirements
steps.detail: Subscribe to the compliance webhooks. Add the app icon, the API contact details and an emergency developer contact in the app's submission setup.

steps.title: Submit the app for App Store review
steps.detail: Open the Shopify App Store review page in the Partner Dashboard. Fill in the mandatory fields and fix anything the automated checks flag, then submit. Your protected customer data request must already be filed.

steps.title: Wait for Shopify's review
steps.detail: The app moves through Draft, Submitted, Reviewed and Published. Shopify emails status updates and shows them in the Partner Dashboard. Shopify may also select the app for a detailed data protection review and ask for evidence of compliance. The documentation gives no turnaround time, so the duration here is a guess.

steps.title: Go live on merchant stores
steps.detail: Once the app is published and protected customer data is approved, install it on a real merchant store. Check that order fields return real values instead of null. Verify the granted scopes and make sure the app handles THROTTLED responses.

risks.title: Order data comes back null without protected customer data approval
risks.symptom: HTTP 200 with null customer fields and an errors entry: "This app is not approved to access the Customer object."
risks.fix: Request protected customer data access in the Partner Dashboard and complete the Data protection details. Request only the fields you need.

risks.title: Protected customer data cannot be requested while the app is under review
risks.fix: File the protected customer data request before you submit the app for review.

risks.title: read_orders only returns the last 60 days of orders
risks.symptom: Older orders are missing from SHOPIFY_LIST_ORDERS results.
risks.fix: If the assistant needs older orders, declare read_all_orders alongside read_orders. It does nothing on its own and needs Shopify approval, which would raise the review burden.

risks.title: Merchants can change the scopes at authorization
risks.symptom: The token comes back with fewer scopes than you declared.
risks.fix: Check the granted scopes in the token response before storing the token, and prompt the merchant to reinstall if any are missing.

risks.title: Public distribution is a permanent choice
risks.fix: Decide between public and custom distribution before you create the app. You cannot change it afterwards.

risks.title: New public apps must use expiring offline access tokens
risks.symptom: Access tokens expire and requests fail until you refresh them.
risks.fix: Exchange the authorization code with expiring=1 and store the refresh token. Check that your Composio auth config handles refreshing.

risks.title: REST endpoints may be rejected for new public apps (unconfirmed)
risks.fix: Confirm whether the two Composio tools call REST or GraphQL Admin API endpoints. If you build custom calls, use GraphQL.

risks.title: API rate limits throttle bulk order reads
risks.symptom: GraphQL returns a THROTTLED error, possibly with HTTP 200. REST returns HTTP 429.
risks.fix: Back off and retry. Limits apply per app and store pair and depend on the store's plan. Use pagination and keep each query's cost low.

risks.title: Review turnaround is not documented
risks.fix: Plan for a multi-week wait and submit early. Use a development store for demos and testing while you wait.

openQuestions: How long does Shopify's App Store review take, and how long does protected customer data approval take? The retrieved docs give no turnaround time.
Does the Composio shopify toolkit support custom auth configs with your own client ID and secret? Does it handle expiring offline tokens and refresh tokens?
Will this be used on one merchant's store only? If so, custom distribution might avoid App Store review, but we found no source on its review or protected customer data requirements.
Does the assistant need orders older than 60 days? That would require read_all_orders and Shopify approval.
Which order fields does the assistant need? Name, address, phone or email fields are Level 2 and need individual approval.
Do SHOPIFY_LIST_ORDERS and SHOPIFY_GET_PRODUCTS use REST or GraphQL endpoints, given the unconfirmed GraphQL-only requirement for new public apps?
The probe at api.shopify.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returned metadata (tp1), but its relation to the merchant install flow is unclear. Other well-known endpoints returned 404.
Does creating a Dev Dashboard app require a Shopify Partner account? The fetched docs do not say.
